brief: Goldman's daily cross-asset wrap (27 Oct) notes the S&P rose about 70bp to 7677 (+12% YTD) on low volume with signs of AI stabilization, SOX up 2.8%, while Bovespa fell 14% after Lula's election. GS expects the FOMC to skip a hike at tomorrow's meeting but deliver a second hike in December. Broadcom, SpaceX and Meta's recent fundraising adds roughly $198bn more, underscoring AI capex funding needs; GS ties AI-linked borrowing, deficits and central-bank hikes to a ~100bp rise in DM yields since early 2026, which it estimates will cut cumulative GDP by 0.6% via weaker housing, consumer durables and business investment. Central bankers increasingly cite the AI buildout as an inflation driver through memory prices, electronics and power costs, though GS views the net inflation impact as limited. Microsoft is offering buyouts to about 60k staff (25% of headcount) after cutting 15k last year. GS likes buying the dip in Greek banks (GSXEGRBK, down ~15%), lowers its Kospi target from 12k to 9k while still calling Korea undervalued, and notes CoreWeave does not need unsecured debt.
